**Probably yes, but it is not yet confirmed.**

- **Loss detected:** Hansen data show 13.5 ha of tree-cover loss in 2025, about 3.9% of the 345.6 ha property.
- **Forest status:** The JRC map shows 98% of the affected area was forest in 2020. The 2021 national forest map classes 13.1 ha as native forest and none as planted. The remaining 0.4 ha lies outside mapped forest.
- **Why it is unconfirmed:** The corroboration rule requires a later year of data showing the loss persisted. The loss falls in 2025, the latest year available, so no later year exists to check it. The JRC agreement meets the rule's threshold, but the temporal check cannot yet be met.

Treat this as a likely native forest loss of about 13 ha that needs confirmation once 2026 data are available. The engine is also an early-access version.
